model_annotation: The figure presents two line plots comparing the training reward performance of two reinforcement learning methods—“Llama-On-Policy” and “Llama-LUFFY”—on “Easy” and “Hard” training sets, respectively. In the top plot (“Easy Training Set”), the x-axis represents training steps from 0 to 500 (linear scale), and the y-axis shows training rewards ranging from 0.0 to 0.4. The “Llama-On-Policy-Easy” method (teal line with shaded confidence interval) starts near 0.0, rises steadily to approximately 0.35 by step 200, and fluctuates slightly around 0.35–0.4 thereafter. The “Llama-LUFFY-Easy” method (red line with shaded interval) follows a similar trajectory, beginning near 0.0, reaching ~0.35 by step 200, and stabilizing near 0.4 with minor fluctuations. In the bottom plot (“Hard Training Set”), the x-axis again spans 0 to 500 steps, while the y-axis ranges from 0.0 to 0.2. The “Llama-On-Policy-Hard” method (teal) begins near 0.0, rises to ~0.05 by step 100, then plateaus near 0.0 before declining slightly. In contrast, “Llama-LUFFY-Hard” (red) starts near 0.0, climbs steadily to ~0.15 by step 300, and continues rising to ~0.2 by step 500, showing consistent improvement. Both plots include shaded regions around each line indicating variability or confidence intervals.
